target_customer: Airlines and ferry operators; defense customers (US Marine Corps contracts, REGENT Defense)
problem: Regional coastal transport is slow and costly, and electric aircraft range is short; a wing-in-ground-effect craft regulated as a maritime vessel could fly farther per charge at lower cost.
business_model: Hardware sales of seagliders (Viceroy, Squire, Monarch) to operators with orders and deposits, plus defense contracts

founders.name: Mike Klinker
education: MIT, BS/MS aircraft controls and autonomy

technical_complexity.rationale: A new vehicle class: wing-in-ground craft with float, foil and fly modes, electric propulsion, and a new certification path; seed-stage TRL 5 in 2021 and the first crewed flight came only in Sept 2026.

defensibility.rationale: Hard-to-replicate engineering, a Coast Guard maritime certification path and a 255,000 sq ft factory create barriers; legacy wing-in-ground craft, seaplanes and eVTOL are the alternative categories.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied or bought the wedge in the sources found; Lockheed Martin and Japan Airlines became investors instead.

market_need_then: Electric aircraft range was limited by batteries; Thalheimer's 2021 paper claimed 180 miles with existing batteries and up to 500 miles with next-generation batteries for coastal routes such as Boston to New York and inter-island Hawaii.

branding.name_origin: Acronym; the company FAQ expands it as Regional Electric Ground Effect Nautical Transport (Built In in 2021 wrote 'naval').
branding.domain_note: Uses regentcraft.com, not regent.com (the plain word is common); acquisition story not found.

identity.logo: REGENT logo variants (full color, white, blue, light) in the media kit
identity.voice_and_tone: Precise brand rules: REGENT in capitals, Seaglider capitalized as a new vehicle class, product names Viceroy, Squire, Monarch

branding.brand_signature: The Seaglider category name, with a pending SEAGLIDER trademark filing
branding.community_and_virality: Wide trade-press and video coverage of the first crewed flight (Sept 2026); no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: A distinct category term (Seaglider) and royal product names help press pick-up, but the plain word REGENT is common and the evidence of brand-driven growth is thin.

outcome_analysis: REGENT, founded in late 2020 by two MIT aerospace engineers, raised a $9M seed in April 2021, a $60M Series A in October 2023 and a $240M Series B in August 2026 (half debt), and flew a crewed Viceroy for the first time on September 2, 2026. Original timelines slipped (prototype tests were planned for 2023 and service for 2025; manufacturing is now targeted for 2027), but investors, strategic partners, Marine Corps contracts and a built factory show strong momentum while commercial revenue is still ahead.
notes: The Series B is about $120M equity and $120M debt per the company release; amount_usd records the full $240M. The earlier depth-1 record listed a different investor set (Alaska Airlines, Mesa, NEOM and others) with only the company site as source; those names were not found in the release and were removed. Company claims more than $10B in global commercial orders and $340M raised across equity and debt; these are company claims, whether orders are binding is not stated. ZoomInfo's $87M total and Lockheed lead and an $18M 2022 round are unverified and not recorded. Valuation is undisclosed; PitchBook $192M (2024) and Multiples $120M (2023) conflict and are not recorded. Dated competition near April 2021: none found in the sources (Built In names none), so the list is empty.
